results.title: Develop and integrate AI agents with Google Workspace
results.content:
[0:47] Think about it.
[0:48] What if you could have your own agent in a CLI, automatically update drive files with the latest documentation as you work on issues?
[0:57] What if you could have your own agent that processes incoming Gmail messages for urgent requests and automatically blocks time in calendar.
[1:07] What if your organization could provide an agent that monitors Google Docs and notifies people in Google Chat, depending on their roles.
[1:15] Well, Google Workspace and Google AI make that possible.
[1:21] Google's AI ecosystem is made of several layers that span from infrastructure to agents and applications.
[1:28] That makes it possible for anyone to integrate solutions of any shape from anywhere. You are a user? Use pre-built agents. [...] [9:54] It comes with governance for security and control, and it supports all kinds of agents, agents developed using no-code, low-code, pro-code tools,
[10:04] agents authored by Google, the organization partners, or third parties, and agents that can run from anywhere, whether they are built using Google's AI tech stack or not.
[10:16] In the Cloud Console, admins can set up data stores.
[10:20] Here is an example of Workspace data stores connected to a Gemini enterprise app.
[10:27] Admins can also register agents running from any agent platform, using the agent-to-agent protocol or the Cloud Marketplace.
[10:37] These agents can use tools based on Workspace APIs or Google-managed MCPs and rely on the authentication mechanism of Gemini enterprise. [...] [5:02] You can use a no-code approach with AppSheet, a low-code approach with Apps Script, and a pro-code approach with any other tech stack.
[5:12] There are extensive APIs and libraries to retrieve data and take actions on behalf of users, such as accessing Gmail messages or creating calendar events.
[5:23] In this particular example, I have an Agent Development Kit function tool that creates calendar events for users.
[5:32] Most Workspace application UIs are extendable using add-ons. So it's possible to meet the users where they are.
[5:40] In this case, the user opens the sidebar in Gmail to ask their travel concierge agent to plan their trip based on the information in the message that's currently open.

Choose tools and connectors: Select the approved apps the agent can use to complete the workflow. You can also describe the systems the agent needs to access, and the builder will guide you through adding and authenticating them.

3.   Choose a trigger: Decide when the agent should run. An agent trigger is the event that starts the agent running. For workspace agents, it can be human-triggered (someone asks it to do something), schedule-triggered (it runs at a set time). You can use the agent builder chat to set up your trigger using plain language.

4.   Add guardrails: Set boundaries, required approvals, and any human-in-the-loop checkpoints for sensitive actions. You can add these directly into the agent builder chat, and the agent builder will modify the instructions.
